newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-RICHTER RECORDS THIRD SHUTOUT AS RANGERS BLANK DEVILS.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-RICHTER RECORDS THIRD SHUTOUT AS RANGERS BLANK DEVILS.

text.p: Mike Richter stopped all 33 shots he faced to record his third shutout of the season as the New York Rangers blanked the New Jersey Devils 3-0 on Sunday.
Mark Messier broke in alone and beat Martin Broduer just 3:18 into the first period with his 25th goal to provide Richter with all the offence he would need.
Rookie Vladimir Vorobiev picked up an assist on the goal on his first shift in the NHL.
Wayne Gretzky set up insurance goals by Ulf Samuelsson and Luc Robitaille in a 1:54 span early in the third period.
Richter made 26 saves over the final two periods to preserve his 17th career shutout.
"Richter made some key saves at the right time on some screen shots," said Rangers coach Colin Campbell. "Tonight, we got the lead early and hung on."
In two games against the Devils this season, Richter has stopped 86 of 87 shots and the Rangers have outscored New Jersey 9-1.
"We're getting good chances, we're not putting the puck in. It's hard to win when you don't score goals," said Devils captain Scott Stevens.
In Phoenix, Jason Dawe scored off a turnover just 10 seconds into overtime to lift the Buffalo Sabres to a 3-2 victory over the Coyotes.
Phoenix's Dave Manson picked up the puck just outside his own blue line, but tripped over a linesman's skate and lost control of the puck, allowing Dawe to take possession.
Dawe broke in and put a wrist shot over goaltender Nikolai Khabibulin's left shoulder for the game-winner.
Brian Holzinger and Mike Peca also scored for the Sabres.

Dominik Hasek made 32 saves for Buffalo, allowing goals by Keith Tkachuk and Igor Korolev, whose powerplay tally in the third tied the game just 42 seconds after Peca's short-handed goal had given Buffalo a 2-1 lead.
In Edmonton, Mats Lindgren scored a powerplay goal 2:27 into overtime as the Oilers beat the Hartford Whalers 2-1, handing them their ninth straight road loss.
Hartford's Steven Rice was called for hooking 69 seconds into overtime, giving Edmonton its seventh power play.
Doug Weight unleashed a wrist shot that Lindgren deflected from the slot past goaltender Sean Burke for the victory.
Weight had given the Oilers a 1-0 lead with a powerplay goal 7:54 into the game. Adam Burt tied it for Hartford at 6:16 of the second.
Curtis Joseph made 27 saves for Edmonton and did not face a shot in overtime.
In Vancouver, Paul Kariya scored a powerplay goal midway through the second period to lift the Mighty Ducks of Anaheim to a 3-2 victory over the Canucks.
Brian Bellows and Teemu Selanne had the other goals for the Ducks. Selanne has 25 for the season.
Kariya's game-winner atoned for a costly mistake earlier in the contest when a bad pass led to a short-handed goal by Vancouver's Mike Sillinger that tied the game 2-2 at 8:55 of the second period.
Vancouver's Kirk McLean made 38 saves in a losing effort as the Ducks outshot the Canucks 41-23.
